ph: The first satsangi tribal graduate being garlanded by Swamishri, Dharampur, 4 May 1999

w: In the evening, Swamishri visited the BAPS Gurukul and high School.

In the evening assembly, the Sargam Club of Rajkot organized a program to honor Swamishri. Fifty-four distinguished organizations in Rajkot honored Swamishri as a torchbearer of Indian culture. The State Finance Minister Shri Vajubhai Vala and Central Minister for Human Resources Shri Vallabhbhai Kathiriya spoke glowingly of Swamishri's divine personality. A citation of honor was presented to Swamishri. Finally, Swamishri addressed the assembly of 7,000 devotees and well-wishers.

Swamishri observed the lunar eclipse from 7.45 p.m. During the program of dhun and bhajans Swamishri said the rosary. Thereafter Viveksagar Swami talked about the eclipse from the Indian scriptural perspective. Finally Swamishri blessed the assembly and after the lunar eclipse Swamishri bathed and performed his personal puja.

st.t: Chandra Grahan - Lunar Eclipse - Tuesday 4 May 2004
w: Devotees in London observed the lunar eclipse in the presence of Pramukh Swami Maharaj on the evening of Tuesday 4th May 2004, commencing with dhun and kirtans at 7.45pm. Swamishri, present in the haveli from the opening, signalled his personal intent for the evening with a delightful gesture, throwing his arms aloft in the air encouraging sadhus and devotees to sing devotional songs with emotion.

Ghanshyamcharan Swami provided an entertaining discussion on the fruits of religious discourses, with an array of kirtans. Krishnapriya Swami rose to the occasion by continuing the lively kirtans. Swamishri’s eyes illustrated his enjoyment as the sparkling smile and memorable laugh illuminated the evening.

Swamishri was adorned with an orange shawl as the evening progressed past 10pm with dimmed lights providing a majestic image in preparation of the chestha, chanted together by the entire sabha. Such breathtaking darshan of Swamishri imprinted a stunning murti in the hearts of all.

Following Viveksagar Swami’s brief discourse of the observance of this eclipse, Swamishri offered his blessings, emphasising the importance of observing such religious occasions and explained the significance of such festivals as established by Bhagwan Swaminarayan. Swamishri thanked the attendees for their devotion. Praising the sadhus and devotees for their contribution to a marvellous evening, Swamishri concluded his blessings shortly before 11.15pm when the final dhun was chanted.

After having darshan up in the mandir, Pramukh Swami Maharaj came to the circumambulation path of the mandir. Sadhus, parshads and sadhaks from abroad, sitting in the Rupchoki, began to sing together the kirtan "Mohanne gamva ne ichchho manni". In it came the words "Manni tek jo..." (the mind's insistence).
"What does tek mean?" Swamishri asked them.
"To give up the mind's insistence means to give up what the mind wants."
"That is right. Give up the mind's beliefs. We are Brahman, we are the atma, we are Akshar. Let others say whatever they want to say, but we should make this belief firm."
Three brothers came for darshan. Knowing their background, Pramukh Swami Maharaj listened to them and then said, "Do you serve your mother or not? Serve your mother well."
They said, "Bapa! We do call her to our home, but she does not like living with us in the city, so after a while she goes to her son-in-law's. But we do give her all her expenses."
Swamishri asked in detail how much they gave her for expenses and said, "If she does not like being in your home, it does not matter, but whenever there is need, keep giving her extra money too."

Pramukh Swami Maharaj, who had come up to the mandir for darshan, came onto the circumambulation path. The sadhus, parshads and seekers from abroad sitting in the rupchoki (mandir porch) began singing together the pad "Mohanne gamva ichchho manni". In it came the words "Manni tek jo..."
"What does 'tek' mean?" Swamishri asked them.
"Giving up the tek of the mind means giving up what the mind has set itself on."
"That is right. Give up the beliefs of the mind. We are Brahma, we are the atma, we are Akshar. Let others say what they want, but we must strengthen this belief."
Three brothers came for darshan. Knowing their background, Pramukh Swami Maharaj listened to what they had to say and then said, "Do you serve your mother or not? Serve your mother properly."

They said, "Bapa! We do invite her home, but she is not comfortable living with us in the city, so after a little while she goes off to her son in law's house. But we certainly give her all her expenses."
Swamishri asked in detail how much they gave for her expenses and said, "If she does not like it at home, that is all right, but whenever there is need, keep giving extra money for her expenses too."

The sadhus, parshads and sadhaks from abroad sitting in the Rupchowki began to sing together the verse "Mohanne gamva ne ichchho manni" (If you wish to please Mohan, O mind). "What does tek mean?" Swamishri asked them.
"To give up the stubbornness of the mind, that is, to give up acting by the mind's wishes."
"That is right. Give up the beliefs of the mind. We are Brahman, we are the atma, we are Akshar. Let others say what they want, but we should make this belief firm."

After coming up to the mandir for darshan, Swamishri went round the mandir in pradakshina. In the rupchoki, sadhus, parshads and sadhaks from abroad began singing together the pad 'Mohanne gamvane ichchho manni'. In it came the words, 'Manni tek jo...'
"What does tek mean?" Swamishri asked them.
"Giving up the mind's tek means giving up what the mind insists on."
"That is right. Give up the mind's beliefs. We are Brahman, we are the soul, we are Akshar. Let others say what they want, but we must make this belief firm."

They said, "Bapa! We do invite her home, but she is not comfortable living with us in the city, so after a while she goes to her son in law's home. But we do pay all her expenses."
Swamishri asked in detail how much they gave and said, "If she does not like living in your home, that is fine, but whenever there is need, keep giving extra money too."

A devotee from Dholka came for darshan. This devotee, who lives in a village next to Dholka, and his wife walk to the Dholka mandir every month on Purnima (full moon day) so that their two or three year old son will grow up, become educated and become a sadhu. Pramukh Swami Maharaj was pleased with this devotee's faith and devotion.
When Pramukh Swami Maharaj is giving meetings to everyone, if small infants have come for darshan, special arrangements are made for them. Those infants are seated on the table.

Today two infants were sitting for Swamishri's darshan. One infant was quiet and the other restless and naughty. As per the custom, the sadhus gave one box of prasad. This box was in the hands of the quiet infant. Seeing this, the restless infant crawled over again and again to try to snatch the box. Seeing the antics of this infant, who could not even speak yet, Swamishri burst out laughing and said loudly to Vimalprakash Swami, the sadhu in charge standing in front, "Hey, give this one another box of prasad." Swamishri stayed right there until the box was given. After the infant got the box, Swamishri moved on with the meetings.

ds.t: A pilgrimage on foot each full moon
w: A devotee had come from Dholka for darshan. This devotee, who lives in a village near Dholka, and his wife walk every full moon to the Dholka mandir so that their two or three year old son may grow up, study and become a sadhu. Pramukh Swami Maharaj was pleased with the faith and devotion of this devotee.
When Pramukh Swami Maharaj is giving meetings to everyone, special arrangements are made for little children who come for darshan. These children are seated on a table.

Today two little children were sitting for Swamishri's darshan. One child was quiet and the other restless and naughty. As usual, the sants gave a box of prasad. This box was in the quiet child's hands. As soon as he saw this, the restless child crawled over again and again and tried to snatch the box. Seeing the antics of this child, who could not yet even speak, Swamishri burst out laughing and said loudly to Vimalprakash Swami, the sant in charge standing in front, "Hey there, give this one another box of prasad." Swamishri stayed right there until the box was given. Only after the child had got the box did Swamishri move on with the meetings.

Today, after finishing breakfast, as Mahant Swami Maharaj was walking a hundred steps, Brahmviharidas Swami said, "'The biggest challenge today is not war but the tendency to be negative.' Research says that more people have died from negativity than have died in wars."
Giving a direct solution, Swamishri said, "The remedy for removing negativity is this: 'In the joy of others lies our own.' And the second is seeing others as faultless."
